ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB \parallel CD$, $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point P. E and F are the midpoints of $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. If $AB = 10$ and $CD = 6$, what is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect CF and extend it to meet AB at G, \\
$\because$AB$\parallel$DC, \\
$\therefore$$\angle$D＝$\angle$B, \\
$\because$F is the midpoint of BD, \\
$\therefore$DF＝BF, \\
In $\triangle DFC$ and $\triangle BFG$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle D=\angle B \\ DF=BF \\ \angle DFC=\angle BFG\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$$\triangle DFC\cong \triangle BFG$ by ASA, \\
$\therefore$BG＝CD＝6, CF＝FG, \\
$\therefore$AG＝AB−BG＝4, \\
$\because$CF＝FG, CE＝EA, \\
$\therefore$EF＝$\frac{1}{2}$AG＝$\frac{1}{2}\times 4＝\boxed{2}$

In $\triangle DFC$ and $\triangle BFG$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle D=\angle B \\ DF=BF \\ \angle DFC=\angle BFG\end{array}\right.$, $\therefore \triangle DFC\cong \triangle BFG$ by ASA, $\therefore BG=CD=6$, $CF=FG$, $\therefore AG=AB-BG=4$, $\because CF=FG$, $CE=EA$, $\therefore EF=\frac{1}{2}AG=\frac{1}{2}\times 4=\boxed{2}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, below is the longer horizontal line segment AB, with A at the lower left and B at the lower right; above is the shorter horizontal line segment CD, with D at the upper left and C at the upper right, and CD is parallel to AB. The oblique lines AC and BD intersect at point P; E lies on AC and F lies on BD, and the given conditions state that E and F are respectively the midpoints of AC and BD. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let A=(0,0), B=(10,0). Because CD is parallel to AB, and CD=6, we may set D=(t,h), C=(t+6,h), where t represents the horizontal translation of the upper base relative to the lower base, and h represents the height. E is the midpoint of AC, so E=((0+t+6)/2,(0+h)/2)=((t+6)/2,h/2). F is the midpoint of BD, so F=((10+t)/2,(0+h)/2)=((t+10)/2,h/2). Therefore the y-coordinates of E and F are the same, and EF is the horizontal distance: EF=((t+10)/2)-((t+6)/2)=4/2=2.
